'''Henrique Gomes de Paiva Lins de Barros''' (May 30, 1947 – September 28, 2025) was a Brazilian physicist, [[Biophysics|biophysicist]], writer, [[Science communication|science communicator]] specialist,<ref name=Fio/> musician, screenwriter, painter and poet.<ref name=Fapesp/>

==Early life==
Lins de Barros was born on May 30, 1947. His parents were Henry British (a Navy official<ref name=Fapesp/>) and Eurydice Gomes de Paiva Lins de Barros.<ref name=Gene/> His father and uncles participated in the creation of the [[Centro Brasileiro de Pesquisas Físicas|Centro Brasileiro de Pesquisas Físicas (CBPF)]],<ref name=Fapesp/> along with [[César Lattes]], one of the founding members<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://revistapesquisa.fapesp.br/dialogo-equacionado/|title=Diálogo equacionado|language=pt-br|author=Rodrigo de Oliveira Andrade|date=March 2007|access-date=May 4, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210115173903/https://revistapesquisa.fapesp.br/dialogo-equacionado/|archive-date=January 15, 2021|url-status=live}}</ref> and a friend of the Lins de Barros family.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.unicamp.br/unicamp/unicamp_hoje/ju/marco2005/ju281pag7a.html|title=O insondável e as razões da coincidência|language=pt-br|author=Henrique Lins de Barros|date=2005|access-date=May 4, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050404021020/https://www.unicamp.br/unicamp/unicamp_hoje/ju/marco2005/ju281pag7a.html|archive-date=April 4, 2005|url-status=live}}</ref> Raised in [[Copacabana, Rio de Janeiro|Copacabana]] in an apartment "where we almost couldn't see the sky",<ref name="OMA" /> he and his brothers developed an interest in airplanes and learned to recognize them by their sound.

==Career==
In 1964, Lins de Barros began studying engineering at the [[Fluminense Federal University]], switching after eighteen months to physics at [[Pontifical Catholic University of Rio de Janeiro|PUC-RJ]] before graduating in 1970. During this time, he began creating music as a hobby.<ref name=Fapesp/> He received a master's degree in atomic theory in 1973,<ref name="Fio">{{Cite web |title=O homem que sabia voar |url=http://www.fiocruz.br/brasiliana/cgi/cgilua.exe/sys/start.htm?infoid=92&sid=31 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210502221139/http://www.fiocruz.br/brasiliana/cgi/cgilua.exe/sys/start.htm?infoid=92&sid=31 |archive-date=May 2, 2021 |access-date=May 2, 2020 |language=pt-br}}</ref> and also worked as a teacher there.<ref name=OMA/>

He earned a doctorate in Physics from the [[Centro Brasileiro de Pesquisas Físicas|Brazilian Center for Research in Physics]] in 1978 and served as its director from {{ill|Museu de Astronomia e Ciências Afins|pt|Museu de Astronomia e Ciências Afins}}, 1992–2000.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://buscatextual.cnpq.br/buscatextual/visualizacv.jsp?id=K4727226Z3|title=Henrique Gomes de Paiva Lins de Barros|language=pt-br|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080828073801/http://buscatextual.cnpq.br/buscatextual/visualizacv.jsp?id=K4727226Z3|archive-date=August 28, 2008|url-status=dead|access-date=May 3, 2021}}</ref> In 1989, he developed an exposition about 20th-century scientific questions.<ref name=Fio/> At the CBPF, he worked in the field of biophysics,<ref name=Fio/> and a joint investigation with UFRJ resulted in the discovery of a multicellular bacterium.<ref name=Fapesp>{{Cite web|url=https://revistapesquisa.fapesp.br/do-atomo-ao-aviao/|title=Henrique Lins de Barros: Do átomo ao avião|language=pt-br|author=Neldson Marcolin|date=August 2007|edition=137|access-date=May 2, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200925225829/https://revistapesquisa.fapesp.br/do-atomo-ao-aviao/|archive-date=September 25, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref>

His research interests include [[atomic physics]], [[biophysics]], the [[history of science]] and technology. He considered himself an experimentalist rather than a theorist.<ref name=Fapesp/>

===Science communication===
Lins de Barros began as a science communicator during the [[Brazilian military dictatorship]] in the 1980s and participated in conferences.<ref name=Fio/> Unable to balance his academic work with his science communication efforts, he discontinued his scholarly work.<ref name=Fio/>

===Santos-Dumont===
Lins de Barros was considered an expert on the life and work of [[Alberto Santos Dumont]], having written four books about the Brazilian aviator and is considered a reference in Brazil and worldwide.<ref name=Fio/><ref name=Fapesp/> His interest in Santos Dumont began in the 1980s when he saw a replica of the 1909 [[Santos-Dumont Demoiselle|Demoiselle]]. He began researching Dumont and his plane, aiming to create a small-scale replica for himself. He also disputed the notion that the [[Wright Brothers]] invented the airplane, asserting that the controversy in Brazil reflects a failure of Brazilian science communication.<ref name=Fio/> According to him, political pressure favors discussing the Wrights, and a clear campaign occurred in the late 1930s on behalf of the Americans, despite it lacking "any historical basis," because the brothers never "understood what it is to takeoff," according to the researcher.<ref name=OMA/>

With [[CNPq]] investment, he traveled to France in 1985 to research Santos Dumont for a film project by [[Tizuka Yamasaki]]. Compiling the data, he wrote his first book, "Santos-Dumont," in 1986.<ref name=Fapesp/> The movie was ultimately scrapped due to budget constraints, but he was the screenwriter and composer of the {{ill|Nelson Hoineff|pt|Nelson Hoineff}} documentary, "O homem pode voar" (2003).<ref name=Fio/><ref name=Fapesp/>

In 2005, he participated in the construction of a [[14-bis]] replica by Alan Calassa.<ref name=Fapesp/> In 2014, he took office as chief of the Museum of Environment.<ref name=MMA/>

==Death==
Lins de Barros died on September 28, 2025, at the age of 78.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gov.br/cbpf/pt-br/assuntos/noticias/cbpf-lamenta-o-falecimento-de-henrique-lins-de-barros|title=CBPF lamenta o falecimento de Henrique Lins de Barros|date=2025-09-28|accessdate=2025-09-29|website=Gov|language=pt-br}}</ref>

==Awards==
For his research on Santos Dumont, Henrique Lins de Barros was awarded the [[Order of Aeronautical Merit (Brazil)|Order of Aeronautical Merit]] as [[Order of Aeronautical Merit (Brazil)#Grades|Grand-Officer]]
on October 23, 2007. He also received the [[Santos-Dumont Merit Medal]] and the [[National Order of Scientific Merit]],<ref name=OMA>{{Cite web|url=https://portal.cbpf.br/pt-br/ultimas-noticias/o-menino-que-escutava-avioes-entrevista-com-henrique-lins-de-barros|title=Henrique Lins de Barros, do CBPF, é agraciado com a Ordem do Mérito Aeronáutico no grau de Grande-Oficial|language=pt-br|date=October 25, 2017|access-date=May 2, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210502225848/https://portal.cbpf.br/pt-br/ultimas-noticias/o-menino-que-escutava-avioes-entrevista-com-henrique-lins-de-barros|archive-date=May 2, 2021|url-status=live}}</ref> ''Medalha 20 anos da Ciência Hoje''.<ref name=MMA>{{Cite web|url=http://www.revistahcsm.coc.fiocruz.br/fisico-henrique-lins-de-barros-assume-a-chefia-do-museu-do-meio-ambiente/|title=Físico Henrique Lins de Barros assume a chefia do Museu do Meio Ambiente|language=pt-br|date=January 2014|access-date=May 2, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190806040033/http://www.revistahcsm.coc.fiocruz.br/fisico-henrique-lins-de-barros-assume-a-chefia-do-museu-do-meio-ambiente/|archive-date=August 6, 2019|url-status=live}}</ref>
